scope: Define a narrow RemoteTaskAuthenticator result containing trusted issuer and audience, original principal and current actor, sender-key thumbprint, token expiry, task ceiling and an internal server-resolved task scope.

source_requirements.title: Verify sender proof at the actual remote resource boundary
source_requirements.original_acceptance_criteria:
A properly bound token and proof reaches the existing permitted read/proposal path; the same token without a proof or with a different sender key is rejected before resource access.
Wrong method, target URI, token hash, token audience, expired proof, disallowed algorithm and an untrusted proxy-origin substitution are rejected with bounded, non-secret diagnostics.
A proof-valid request with a changed amount, query resource or proposed action still undergoes existing permission, schema, policy and exact-preview checks; sender proof grants no business approval.

goals.outcome: Require a valid sender-bound token and a fresh proof on each supported remote request, with no bearer downgrade.
scope: Use the selected library for issuer-token verification and cryptographic proof verification. Enforce trusted token confirmation, asymmetric proof algorithm, dpop+jwt type and the public proof key's thumbprint match.

Validate the RFC 9449 method and target-URI binding, access-token hash, proof time and nonce when the selected profile requires it. Derive the effective URL from configured origin/proxy trust; ignore untrusted forwarded-host rewrites.

Keep token audience verification distinct from proof target verification. RFC 9449 htu excludes query and fragment; existing gateway and resource validation must independently validate query parameters and request bodies.

Place verification on the origin route, including direct access that bypasses an optional portal. Do not treat a user-agent header, portal visibility or possession of the token as sender authentication.
Keep proof keys outside model prompts, skill files and model-generated code in the provided client. Document that external-client key custody remains the external operator's responsibility.

goals.title: Fence replay, revocation and active work across verifier processes

source_requirements.title: Fence replay, revocation and active work across verifier processes
source_requirements.original_acceptance_criteria:
Two verifier processes race the same valid proof against the shared store: at most one request is admitted. A restart within the proof window does not make the proof reusable.
Revoked membership/session, an expired task, a stop revision and a stale lease generation deny the relevant next operation or renewal even when the token and cryptographic proof are valid.
Replay-store failure denies protected access and records a bounded reason; recovery restores service without accepting retained replays or reopening expired tasks.
An ambiguous synthetic effect followed by an authenticated takeover remains attached to its original operation identity and proceeds through reconciliation without a second send.
source_requirements.contribution: This adopted Rifare target closes only with its exact criteria, mapped worker and formal milestone evidence.

goals.outcome: Make proof replay and current task restrictions effective across concurrent requests, restarts and lease renewal.
scope: Add bounded shared replay admission with an atomic uniqueness decision for the appropriate issuer/sender/proof identifier, retaining entries through the accepted proof window and skew allowance.
Fail closed when replay admission or required current-authority reads are unavailable. Do not fall back to an instance-local Map or silently clear the active replay window on restart.

Reuse current parent-session, membership, policy, configuration, stop and lease-generation checks. Token lifetime, lease renewal and client handoff cannot exceed the original task ceiling or recover revoked scope.
Record minimized denial/admission reasons and references to the current actor, original principal and task. Never persist raw access tokens, proof JWTs or private keys in receipts.
Preserve existing unknown-operation reconciliation semantics: retrying authentication or taking over a lease must not create a fresh identity for an already attempted business effect.

source_requirements.original_acceptance_criteria:
Without an explicitly active mandate capability, a threshold or schedule creates only one explainable PO draft. Repeated observations, open POs and partial receipts cannot duplicate the same uncovered need or authorize a supplier call.
When the optional path is separately qualified, a principal with M11-G06 procurement approval authority approves its versioned mandate terms, preserving required separation of duties. The proposing or executing agent cannot activate or widen it. Each occurrence rechecks current mandate and authorizing authority, fixed merchant/supplier/SKU terms, stock and open-PO evidence, exact purchase preview, approved quantities and atomic per-order/aggregate spend reservations. Covered changes require new approval.
A timeout after supplier acceptance keeps the original mandate occurrence and purchase identity unknown. Its unresolved stock/order commitment and applicable mandate/budget reservations persist across timeout, restart, mandate expiry and later triggers until authoritative reconciliation or cancellation resolves the outcome. Retries reconcile the original identity; another occurrence cannot consume the same committed need or reserved capacity.
Revocation, expiry, changed supplier or price outside approved bounds before dispatch blocks the recurring effect and preserves a draft/exception. The evidence states whether only drafts or actual qualified mandate execution was observed.

source_requirements.original_acceptance_criteria:
The browser remains responsive through loading and cancellation; no model download begins merely because the ordinary commerce view opens, and an unapproved or corrupt artifact never reaches a ready state.
An actual target browser can load, warm and unload the approved pack, or records a concrete unsupported/unavailable reason. A mocked adapter, navigator.gpu presence or successful file download alone cannot qualify inference.
A cache hit verifies artifact identity and still records initialization; cache eviction, interrupted transfer and insufficient storage yield a recoverable state without an uncontrolled re-download loop.
GPU allocation failure, device loss or a CPU fallback that cannot fit the pack leaves the existing manual workflow available and releases resources when possible, with no automatic hosted inference.

source_requirements.original_acceptance_criteria:
The minimal browser module compiles without Node-only commerce, crypto, filesystem, SQLite or Buffer dependencies and matches retained v1 UTF-8 sizing and result-validation behavior on boundary fixtures. The authorized request retains M13 question/answer IDs and exposes no provider secrets or hidden server-only evidence.
A private M13 prepare() object cannot be serialized or copied into browser authority. A server-issued expiring preparation identity governs ingestion; a forged browser payload claiming fixture/live provenance, canonical branding, verified revision or execution is rejected or retained only as a client assertion in the new record kind.
Cross-tenant substitution, changed evidence/question/configuration, expired preparation, revoked ownership or duplicate/conflicting submission cannot create or replace a usable current observation.
The operator sees a labeled shadow suggestion with execution_authorized:false. Ingestion changes no assignment, rule, eligibility, approval, money, stock, notification or business-operation identity and cannot trigger M14 routing.

scope: Reuse the existing DecisionRequest types and validation semantics through the smallest browser-safe extraction. Use the existing case, permission, support-ownership, execution-stop, resource and privacy owners to issue the minimal currently readable input projection and ingest the proposal. Recheck all current bindings at issuance and acceptance, enforce request-byte/result bounds and replay/idempotency controls, and have the server create its own immutable client-observation receipt rather than accepting a client-authored canonical receipt.

A real browser request reaches the image-aware joint decision computation with all requested questions, or the capability stays unqualified. General runtime image support cannot substitute for this observation.

The privacy record covers every enabled customer-media/derivative surface and demonstrates cleanup/export/restore suppression for controlled stores; an old cache cannot repopulate erased server observations.
Unavailable vision or GPU failure preserves a text/manual alternative and requires a current approved destination selection before any remote inference; there is no silent upload or broadened retention.
